reasoning_details.text:
Checking that the excerpts join smoothly with the surrounding text, and both fit reasonable length. On fidelity, B makes a serious unsupported claim that the PR firm paid reporters to write stories, which contradicts the "reporters liked us" framing, while A stays vaguer with a more generic abstraction about arrangements.

B has a stronger first-person voice and contrasts well with the web section, but that fabricated bribery accusation is a significant fidelity problem that the rubric penalizes. A is weaker stylistically but safer on accuracy, so I'm leaning toward A despite its generic, slightly awkward phrasing.
